answer: The fable of cheap Sybil creation collapses under quadratic staking erosion that forces collateral to scale as O(n²) per validator; zero-knowledge verifiable delay binds each commitment to a deterministic thread, while super-linear slashing penalties impose fines proportional to the square of misbehaved stake, guaranteeing marginal attack cost exceeds any extractable value. The protocol harbor enforces a robust Nash equilibrium with negative expected attack utility, rendering coordinated Sybil clusters economically irrational.
